name: Rosewood Washington, D.C.
positioning: Rosewood hotel on Georgetown's C&O Canal, with adjacent historic townhouses and Wolfgang Puck's CUT D.C.
best_for: Travelers who want a base in historic Georgetown
Food lovers drawn to Wolfgang Puck's CUT D.C. and a rooftop bar

facts.text: Rosewood opened on Georgetown's C&O Canal in 2013.
The hotel is at 1050 31st Street NW in Washington, D.C.
CUT D.C. is Wolfgang Puck's steak restaurant at the hotel, with a vegetable and seafood-centric menu.
CUT D.C. highlights farms and fisheries of the Mid-Atlantic region.
CUT by Wolfgang Puck serves brunch on Saturdays and Sundays.
CUT Bar and Lounge offers live music on select days.
Afternoon tea features savory sandwiches, pastries and sweets paired with teas.
Friday night DJs play at the CUT Above rooftop bar.
The Presidential Suite has an entrance foyer, a fireplace and a dining area.
The Rosewood Suite has a living area, a king-size bed, a walk-in closet and views of historic Georgetown.
Rooms have Art Deco decor influences, with marble bathrooms stocked with Diptyque toiletries.
The hotel offers private event venues for small meetings or celebrations.

highlights.text: Historic Georgetown townhouses adjacent to the hotel offer residential-style access to the neighborhood.
CUT Above is a rooftop bar in the heart of Georgetown with views over the capital skyline.
The hotel has an infinity pool.
CUT Bar has a 2,500-bottle stock and a raw seafood counter.
Non-alcoholic beverages in the minibar are free.

considerations.text: CUT Above is a seasonal rooftop.
Food and drink at the hotel are pricey.
WhataHotel notes limited on-site recreational facilities compared to resort properties.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Rosewood Washington, D.C.
